research_question: Does adding independent Classical Sanskrit training material reduce the observed +0.0776 CE held-out Sanskrit regression without degrading English, Hindi, or Code control domains?

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Mean Sanskrit CE in Arm 2 >= Mean Sanskrit CE in Arm 1 - 1.96 * sigma, or control domain regresses by >= 1.96 * sigma.
hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: Mean Sanskrit CE in Arm 2 < Mean Sanskrit CE in Arm 1 - 1.96 * sigma, while global CE <= 4.2900 and control domain deltas <= 1.0 * sigma.

experimental_arms.name: volume_matched_control
experimental_arms.role: Evaluates generic volume scaling vs Sanskrit semantic transfer

controls_and_invariants.architecture: ChakrMicro (3,443,136 parameters, 6 layers, d_model=192, n_heads=6, tied embeddings)

screening_tiers.method: Unicode NFKC normalization + punctuation stripping 8-gram Jaccard

statistical_decision_rules.validated_recovery: Mean(TW-CE_sa(Arm 2)) <= Mean(TW-CE_sa(Arm 1)) - 1.96 * sigma_sa, Global CE <= 4.2900, Hindi CE <= 3.9250, Win rate >= 70%
statistical_decision_rules.partial_recovery_with_drift: Sanskrit improves >= 1.96 * sigma but control domain degrades > 1.0 * sigma
statistical_decision_rules.inconclusive: Sanskrit difference within seed variance (|delta| < 1.96 * sigma)
statistical_decision_rules.catastrophic_regression: Global CE > 4.4789 or validation CE increases > 0.20
